writeup: For the first time this season, the team on top of the power rankings won a game. Defeating a strong Dwerkers team despite Kenneth Walker’s bye week, Last Chance U scored 174.06 points. Waiver pickup Drake Maye led the entire league in scoring with nearly 40 in his first start for the U. WRs Wilson, Washington, and Jamo also had great games. Loveland is still wasting space on the team, but he might be my only weakness.

Almost 200 for Hugh again, and this time he was down a player. Gibbs, Warren, and Watson all made Team of the Week after monster performances. DJ Moore is dealing with an injury and Warren’s output might not continue, but Hugh’s got enough points on the bench to cope.

Luke’s been slowly climbing the rankings since his initial #11, and now he’s cracked the top 3. He’s the hottest team in the league now with 4 wins in a row. The Little Beauties just made a trade that I don’t think favors them, though, and losing Jeanty after Montgomery suffers what looks like a multiple week injury could be bad news.

CeeDee Lamb absolutely sold, snapping Jackson’s win streak. The squad still looks great, as his Ravens played well with Huntley under center. It might be time to look for a new FLEX as Odunze and Shakir have been unreliable thus far.

The Dream Dwerkers couldn’t get it done against Last Chance U. Despite some big games from Kyren, JSN, LaPorta, and Golden, Darnold had a stinker and he had three roster spots combine for 1.7. Jorge might be in need of some roster acquisitions as depth is still an issue. You need regular points to support your stars.

Huge week for Camden. Almost 160 points  in a blowout victory against Greg. Virtually the whole team balled out, but he did see a few more WRs pick up injuries, including Deebo Samuel Sr who he traded for just a few weeks ago. They don’t seem to be serious, but it’s something to watch for.

Kyle’s team is on a good trend after picking up his third win last week. Nabers is doing just fine without Dart, and Egbuka finally had himself a big game. With his 9ers and Warren continuing their strong seasons, Kyle’s got a squad that will win as long as his WRs continue to improve.

It’s been a disappointing season so far for Greg, but I believe his recent trade with Luke is going to turn his year around. He did exactly what any struggling fantasy manager should do: trade away your most valuable player for multiple starters. Usually when that happens, you don’t get players as high-caliber in return as Jeanty and Adams.

As I said in so many words last week, one player can change everything. Johny’s second win comes thanks to Jayden Daniels. The QB put a brace on his arm and Johny on his back and scored 32.26 with 2 long rushing TDs. Tet McMillan is back after his bye week, so the wins could continue if the dynamic duo can carry.

Back to back to back losses since being ranked #1. Quinn was this week’s lowest scorer after failing to surpass Johny’s measly 93.76. Goff had a game again, much better than Herbert, but he had no help. McLaurin’s 12.2 was the best Quinn could muster to support his QB. Chuba was on a bye, and Ladd should back from injury soon, so not all is lost quite yet.

Four straight losses after injuries ruined ESPN’s top rated draft. Puka and Likely had Team of the Week performances, but aside from them Brady had no one. He currently has six players with injury designations, most recently being TreVeyon Henderson with what might be a high ankle sprain.

Another rough week for Rick. Mike Evans went off, but the praise ends there. Injuries and disappointments have shaped Rick’s squad all season thus far, and we’re just a couple weeks away from the midseason mark. Still searching for his first win, Rick has to be looking for a way forward. Recently dropping Drake Maye and rostering two kickers are just a couple mistakes that need to be remedied if he wants to win.
